content: For the first three seasons of The X-Files, the writers kept you guessing, not only with regard to the show’s greater mysteries about aliens, but also about its most intriguing character. The Cigarette Smoking Man, played by William B. Davis, begins the series as a shadowy, silent character in the first episode. He looks on as Agent Dana Scully (Gillian Anderson) is given her not-too-subtle orders to undermine Agent Fox Mulder (David Duchovny) and his work on the X-Files. He goes on to appear sparingly, just a few times each season, to stop Mulder and Scully from getting too close to the secrets he’s spent decades covering up.
